FILE CANDIDATE.md
# Ordinary candidate: MathDB 336969 — zero credit

All s>=1 and integers 0<=a,b<s with gcd(s,a-b)=1. For the literal source-defined core bipartitions C=C_(s|0,a) intersect C_(s|0,b), the arithmetic mean of |lambda|+|mu| is
(s+1)[a(s-a)+b(s-b)+1-s]/12.

Source bindings: arXiv:1709.00079, Conjecture 4.6, Proposition 4.4, Theorem 4.2 and its full proof, beta-set definition 2.4 and Remark in 2.3. Read source text lines 120–168, 190–285, 880–1075, 1190–1239. Current author accepted-manuscript copy, sources/cores-author.pdf, still states Conjecture 4.6 (text1172ff); exact PDF hashes in access inventories. This is an ordinary deduction, not a claim that the manuscript's underlying theorems were independently re-proved or formally checked.

## Parametrization, with normalization paid

First s>1. Put d=b-a, residues in Z/sZ. Let U be uniform among binary vectors of length s with exactly a ones, and V independently uniform among those with b ones. The equations
  y_i=x_(i+a)-a+s U_i=x_(i+b)-b+s V_i                 (1)
uniquely determine x,y up to a common additive constant because d generates Z/sZ. Indeed
  x_(j+d)-x_j=d+s(U_(j-a)-V_(j-a)).                 (2)
The increments around the cycle sum to sd+s(a-b)=0, so consistency holds. Choose the common additive constant to make sum x_i=s(s-1)/2; equation (1) then gives the same sum for y.

The resulting x_i are integers: starting with integral x_0, all x_i are integral and x_i-x_0 congruent i modulo s, hence their sum is congruent s(s-1)/2 modulo s. The normalizing translation is integral. The residues of x_i are i+C for a single integer C; y_i has the same residue i+C by (1). Relabeling index i to i-C makes x and y valid s-sets. Each s-set has distinct residues and normalized sum; by the source s-set/beta-set correspondence it is the s-set of a unique s-core. Proposition 4.4 makes the resulting pair lie in C. Conversely any pair in C gives the two binary vectors through (1), and all the choices producing it are simultaneous cyclic shifts. This is also the explicit bijection proved in Theorem 4.2, rather than an inference from its counting formula alone.

Every cyclic orbit of (U,V) has size s. If a shift of order t>1 fixes both vectors, t divides s,a,b, hence divides d, contrary to gcd(s,d)=1. Consequently uniform independent U,V, followed by forgetting the simultaneous shift, induces the UNIFORM measure on C, not a stabilizer-weighted measure. Sum x_i^2+sum y_i^2 is unchanged by relabeling. This is the required bridge for unweighted average size.

## Partition size from its beta-set

For a normalized s-set with entry z_i congruent i (0<=i<s), write z_i=i+s q_i. Then sum q_i=0. Its beta-set consists on runner i of i+s k for integers k<q_i, versus k<0 for the empty partition. The charge-zero beta-set size formula (sum of added beta numbers minus sum of removed beta numbers) gives
 |lambda|=sum_i [i q_i+s q_i(q_i-1)/2]
          =(sum_i z_i^2-sum_i i^2)/(2s).
For q_i<0 the same formula follows by subtracting the finite progression k=q_i,...,-1, so no positivity restriction was smuggled in. The beta-set formula itself follows by truncating both decreasing beta sequences below a common negative cutoff: lambda_j=beta_j+j and the j terms cancel. Equal charge ensures identical truncation lengths. In particular, with c=(s-1)/2,
 |lambda|=sum_i(z_i-c)^2/(2s)-(s^2-1)/24.          (3)
The same identity applies to y and mu. A normalized residue-complete set produces a beta-set of charge zero (sum q_i=0), bounded above with cofinite negative tail, so it indeed produces a finite partition; closure under subtracting s makes it an s-core. Thus this step does not replace a partition by an arbitrary rational vector.

## Exact second moments for x and y

Set W=a(s-a)+b(s-b). For a uniform weight-a binary vector,
 E U_i=a/s,
 Var U_i=a(s-a)/s^2,
 Cov(U_i,U_j)=-a(s-a)/(s^2(s-1)) for i!=j.
These follow from P(U_i=U_j=1)=a(a-1)/(s(s-1)); they include a=0. The same holds for V with b. Independence yields for Delta_j=d+s(U_(j-a)-V_(j-a)):
 E Delta_j=0, Var Delta_j=W, Cov(Delta_j,Delta_k)=-W/(s-1) for distinct j,k.
A sum along l consecutive edges of the d-cycle has mean zero and square mean
  l W-l(l-1)W/(s-1)=W l(s-l)/(s-1).             (4)
It equals x_(j+l d)-x_j by (2).

For any real vector x of mean c,
 sum_j(x_j-c)^2=(1/(2s))sum_(j,k)(x_j-x_k)^2.
For each l=1,...,s-1 there are exactly s ordered pairs at d-cycle distance l. By (4),
 E sum_j(x_j-c)^2
 = W/[2(s-1)] sum_(l=1)^(s-1) l(s-l)
 = W s(s+1)/12,                               (5)
since sum l(s-l)=s(s^2-1)/6.

It is necessary to compute mu as well; its correlation with lambda cannot simply be ignored. From (1) one derives
 y_(i+d)-y_i=d+s(U_(i+d)-V_i).                  (6)
The U coordinates have merely been cyclically shifted relative to V. Since the vectors are independent uniform fixed-weight subsets, these increments have exactly the same covariance table, so (5) also holds for y. No independence between x and y is asserted or required.

Adding (3) for both partitions and using (5) proves
 E(|lambda|+|mu|)=(s+1)W/12-(s^2-1)/12
                =(s+1)(W+1-s)/12,
the complete required formula.

For s=1, the only allowed a,b are 0,0, and the source explicitly defines C_(1|c)={empty bipartition}, notwithstanding the ordinary content-uniqueness convention at s=1. Its mean size and the formula both equal zero. If the target instead used unmodified uniqueness-of-content at s=1, that would require a separate semantic decision; the present candidate follows the explicit source convention required by MathDB's reference to source-defined C.

## 336510 / 336511: canonical antipalindromes, multiple routes
Source1706.10206v3 §7.2 Conj13/14 matches both literal statements and the27 exceptions; §7.3 concerns leading-zero generalized antipalindromes and cannot substitute for canonical expansions. No mathematical code was used.

For a canonical antipalindrome of length2k with top-half integer u (2^(k-1)<=u<2^k), its exact value is P_k(u)=2^k u+(2^k-1)-rev_k(u). This follows because the low half is the bitwise complement of the reversal of the high half. The leading1 forces trailing0, as required. Consequently every permitted summand is positive and even. Zero is represented by the empty sum, not by silently calling its canonical digit0 an antipalindrome.

First proposed all-length induction: wrap a shorter word w of length2k by 1,w,0. Complement-of-reversal symmetry is preserved and the value becomes2^(2k+1)+2w. But wrapping r summands maps N=sum w_i to 2N+r*2^(2k+1), with the SAME middle length needed for all summands. This covers separated arithmetic bands and does not cover every even integer of the next lengths with r<=4. Arbitrarily padding w with leading zeroes destroys the canonical condition and is exactly the invalid generalized-antipalindrome shortcut.

Second mechanism: use the full P_k(u) freedom, split the desired number into high-half sums and low reversed-half sums. For r summands of common length2k, the exact equation is N=2^k sum u_i+r(2^k-1)-sum rev_k(u_i). Reversal is not an additive homomorphism. Matching high and low halves separately does not ensure simultaneous solutions: carries constrain them. A credible completion would specify finite carry/boundary states for the two-ended digit construction, prove every transition preserves complementary symmetric digits and canonical endpoints, and prove EVERY even input belongs to a state reachable with <=4 summands. For336511 it must additionally prove all nonlisted inputs reachable with<=3, not just that listed E fail. No such invariant/transition coverage proof was found here. The source's conditional13 bound and generalized7 bound do not imply these smaller bounds. This route is parked; no finite search/evidence, no partial-result credit. The2022 companion retrieved is QUOTIENTS of palindromic/antipalindromic numbers, not an additive theorem; its bibliography identifies a materially relevant2020 updated source (Rajasekaran–Shallit–Smith, Additive number theory via automata theory, TCS64,542–567) not read here: precise latest-source HOLD, no denial retry or claim that the2017conjecture remains open today.

## 339332: sacrifice ordering in complete optimal play
Primary1805.09368v3 Definitions1–6,2-action Theorem12 proof portions, §7Conj17 read. The final EJC26(4)2019#P4.52 body has the same question as Conj37 and same example36; journal text source bindings in read inventory. This is not Stewart's already solved periodicity conjecture.

Let O(x)=max_(s in S,s<=x)(s-O(x-s)), terminal O=0, with the source opt convention choosing the LARGEST maximizing s. If first two optimal actions are a and b, and their remaining heap is z=x-a-b, then O(x)=a-b+O(z), O(x-a)=b-O(z). With greedy maximum M legal at both positions, the literal claim about these two sacrifices amounts to M-b<M-a, i.e. a<b. The exact competing-greedy inequalities needed for a counterexample a>=b are
 a-b+O(z)>=M-O(x-M),
 b-O(z)>=M-O(x-a-M),
with STRICT inequalities against a larger maximizing action whenever tie-breaking applies. These constrain different tail values. Bounds0<=O<=M alone do not give a contradiction; summing them loses exactly the tail dependence. This explains why the naive total-score argument fails.

A second route is rearrangement: source Lemma2 permits each player to put their own actions in non-increasing order. It does not compare one player's action to the other's, nor let one exchange actions across players. In particular it cannot turn a>=b into a profitable legal response; the available heap and stopping point change. In the 2-action class the conjecture's antecedent is impossible by source Observation4, so that class is vacuous evidence, not a full proof. Endgame greedy action is max{s<=x}, not always global M; using M at an illegal endgame position would be a false counterexample. A complete finite witness needs a chosen S,x, all relevant O-tail inequalities, the maximal-action tie convention and the exact meaning of multiple sacrifices paid. No witness or full monotonicity theorem was obtained; parked with these explicit gaps. No enumeration program or solver ran.

## 351585: exact relation to351586 and remaining source bridge
Under the MathDB DEFINITION of strongly embeddable as restriction, an arbitrary-rank modular extension gives one of the same rank: if M=N|E, take F=cl_N(E) and N'=N|F. A restriction to a FLAT of a modular matroid is modular, since its flats are precisely the ambient flats contained in F and rank/modular equalities are unchanged. Also r(N')=r_N(E)=r(M). Converse is immediate. Finite N gives finite N'. This is the complete equivalence between the two literal MathDB statements; it is not an exclusion or a claimed new theorem.

Actual Shin2108.04757v1 introduction distinguishes Conj1.1/1.2; Thm5.10 is rank4 and5.11 invokes BK88/Bon11 and HW19. Newly read HW technical report Thm11 and proof preserves rank4, finite ground set and line restrictions; Cor3 passes to rank4 contractions and invokes STRONG embedding as Kantor1974 Definition2 and Theorem2, then Thm17 states global equivalence. Those original strong-embedding hypotheses are not the bare definition supplied by MathDB and Kantor1974body was not read. ## 336855: printed source correction only
Rendered sources/dyck-page3.png confirms Conj2 literally says F but not N intersect D; no lost overbar. Source lemmas5–7 say F=fixpoints, D=fixpoints or deficiencies, N={k:pi^-1(k)>=k}. Hence F is contained in N intersect D and F\(N intersect D) is ALWAYS empty. Double deficiencies are exactly (N intersect D)\F. For example pi=312 avoids321 and k=2 has pi(2)=1<2<pi^-1(2)=3. Source Figure1's second path has r=(-1,0,1,1), c=(1,1,0,-1), N={1,2}, D={2,3}, F=empty; the BJS valley-cross and remaining-increasing-fill rule gives pi312. So the literal refinement fails but the intended reversed-set-difference theorem follows from the paper's own lemmas, as its proof asserts. This is a full wording-correction bridge, not a new significant resolution. It is excluded for credit without silently repairing MathDB.

A class is **strongly rational** if it and all of its subclasses have rational generating functions, and it is **well-quasi-ordered** if its permutations are well-quasi-ordered under pattern containment.\n\n**Strong rationality conjecture.** A permutation class is strongly rational if and only if it is well-quasi-ordered and does not contain the class of $312$-avoiding permutations or any symmetry of it.\n\nThis conjecture seeks to characterize strong rationality using structural properties of permutation classes. The stated results establish the analogous characterization for subclasses of the $321$-avoiding permutations, while the general assertion remains open.",

        "title": "Upper growth rates are realized by sum closed classes",
        "statement": "Let an **upper growth rate** of a permutation class mean a real number that occurs as the upper exponential growth rate of that class, and let a **sum closed class** be a permutation class closed under direct sum. **Upper growth-rate conjecture.** Every upper growth rate of a permutation class is the growth rate of a sum closed class.\n\nThe conjecture would reduce the characterization of upper growth rates to sum closed classes, extending the paper's growth-rate methods.         "statement": "Let $K$ be a quadratic number field, let $f_c(x)=x^2+c$ with $c\\in K$, and let $G(f_c,K)$ be the directed graph of $K$-rational preperiodic points, with an edge $\\alpha\\to f_c(\\alpha)$. **Doyle–Faber–Krumm quadratic-field graph conjecture.** The graph $G(f_c,K)$ is isomorphic to one of the $46$ directed graphs appearing in the cited appendix; in particular, \n$$\n|\\operatorname{PrePer}(f_c,K)|\\leq 15.\n$$\n This is computationally supported and concerns the degree-two case of the quadratic-polynomial uniform boundedness conjecture.         "statement": "For a pattern $\\tau$, let $S_n(\\tau)$ denote the set of permutations in $S_n$ avoiding $\\tau$.         "title": "FindStat's double-deficiency refinement for Dyck paths",
        "statement": "Let $D$ be a Dyck path, let $\\mathcal F$ and $\\mathcal N$ be the statistics defined from its row-area and column-area sequences, and let $\\pi$ be the $321$-avoiding permutation associated with $D$ by the Billey-Jockusch-Stanley bijection. A **double deficiency** is the permutation statistic referenced in the source.\n\n**Double-deficiency refinement.** For a Dyck path $D$, an index $k$ is in $\\mathcal F$ but not in $\\mathcal N\\cap\\mathcal D$ if and only if it is a double deficiency in the $321$-avoiding permutation $\\pi$ associated with $D$ using the Billey-Jockusch-Stanley bijection.\n\nThe source describes this as a common refinement of both parts of Marczinzik's conjecture and proves it using the Billey-Jockusch-Stanley bijection, so it is solved in the paper.",

        "title": "The equal-parameter Armstrong conjecture for simultaneous bicores",
        "statement": "Let $s$ be a positive integer and let $a,b$ satisfy $0\\leq a,b<s$. For parameters $r$ and $c$, write $\\mathcal{C}_{(r\\,|\\,0,c)}$ for the corresponding set of bipartitions, and let the size of a bipartition mean the total number of boxes in its two components. **Equal-parameter Armstrong conjecture.** If $s$ and $a-b$ are coprime, then the average size of a bipartition in\n\n$$\n\\mathcal{C}_{(s\\,|\\,0,a)}\\cap\\mathcal{C}_{(s\\,|\\,0,b)}\n$$\n\nis\n\n$$\n\\frac{(s+1)(a(s-a)+b(s-b)+1-s)}{12}.\n$$\n\nThis is proposed as an analogue of Armstrong's conjecture for simultaneous core bipartitions; the case $a=0$ recovers Armstrong's conjecture for ordinary simultaneous cores.         "title": "A bipartite-subgraph-free bound for pebbling numbers of direct graph products",
        "statement": "Let $G$ and $H$ be connected graphs, with $G\\ne K_1$ and $H$ nonbipartite. Let $G\\times H$ denote the direct product of graphs, and let $\\pi(G)$ denote the pebbling number.\n\n**Direct-product pebbling conjecture.**\n\n$$\n\\pi(G\\times H)\\leq \\frac{9}{16}\\pi(G)\\pi(H)^2.\n$$\n\nThe conjecture seeks to remove the use of chosen connected spanning bipartite subgraphs from the preceding results for direct products. The paper presents the inequality as an expected analogous bound, and it remains unresolved in the source.",

        "title": "Bean–Tannock–Ulfarsson purity conjecture for boundary-grid downcore graphs",
        "statement": "Let $\\pi$ be a $123$-avoiding permutation, and let its boundary grid be the associated skew Young diagram. The **downcore graph** has the boxes of the boundary grid as vertices, with an edge between $(i,j)$ and $(k,\\ell)$ when either $i<k$ and $j>\\ell$, or $i>k$ and $j<\\ell$, and both opposite-corner boxes $(i,\\ell)$ and $(k,j)$ lie in the skew Young diagram. A graph is **pure** if every maximal independent set has the same size. **Bean–Tannock–Ulfarsson's purity conjecture.** The downcore graph of the boundary grid of $\\pi$ is pure if and only if $\\pi$ avoids $2143$. This conjecture concerns a structural characterization of $123$-avoiding permutations through their boundary-grid graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.",
        "statement_completeness": "full",
        "post_type": "conjecture",

        "title": "Extremal hyperedge conjecture for FF4-hypergraphs",
        "statement": "An $FF_{4}$-hypergraph is a $4$-uniform hypergraph in which every set of $5$ vertices contains either $0$ or $2$ hyperedges. Let $\\mathcal{H}$ be an $FF_{4}$-hypergraph with $n$ vertices.\n\n**Extremal hyperedge conjecture.** If $n\\equiv2\\pmod{4}$, then $\\mathcal{H}$ has at most\n\n$$\n\\frac{1}{96}n(n-3)(n+2)(n-2)\n$$\n\nhyperedges. If $n\\equiv1\\pmod{4}$, then $\\mathcal{H}$ has at most\n\n$$\n\\frac{1}{96}(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(n+3)\n$$\n\nhyperedges.\n\nThese bounds arise by deleting two vertices from an $FF_{4}$-design of order $n+2$ when $n\\equiv2\\pmod{4}$, and from one of order $n+3$ when $n\\equiv1\\pmod{4}$. The source presents the bounds as conjectural extremal values; their general validity is not established there.",

        "title": "The mixed-subdivision strengthening of the planar discrete Brunn–Minkowski conjecture",
        "statement": "Let $A,B\\subset\\mathbb R^2$ be finite two-dimensional sets. Let $M$ be a corresponding mixed subdivision of $[A+B]$, and let $M_{11}$ denote the set of parallelograms in $M$. **Mixed-subdivision strengthening.** There exist triangulations $T_A$ and $T_B$ and a corresponding mixed subdivision $M$ such that\n\n$$\n|M_{11}|\\geq \\sqrt{|T_A|\\cdot |T_B|}.\n$$\n\nThis is stated as a stronger version of the planar discrete Brunn–Minkowski conjecture. The parser marks it disproved: the paper gives an example showing that one cannot in general fix the triangulations $T_A$ and $T_B$ in the conjecture.",
